claims.text: The Governor of California announcement metadata records publication at 2026-09-18T15:08:17Z, and signed Executive Order N-9-26 is dated 18 September 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 article:published_time and publishedTime metadata; s2 PDF page 3 signature block

claims.text: Executive Order N-9-26 became effective immediately.
claims.sourceLocator: PDF page 2, paragraph immediately before IT IS HEREBY ORDERED

claims.text: Order paragraph 1 requires Government Operations to complete and publicly post section 8898.1 IVO application requirements, procedures and criteria by 1 May 2027.
SB 813 originally set 1 January 2028 for the section 8898.1 work.
Order paragraph 2 requires Government Operations to complete section 11549.82(a) and begin section 11549.82(b) actions by 1 December 2027.
AB 1405 originally set 1 January 2029 for the registry, fees, misconduct-reporting channel and listed registry actions.
AB 1405 separately keeps 1 January 2029 as the date after which an unregistered person may not offer, sell or conduct a covered AI audit, and the order does not state a new date for that provision.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 section 11549.82.5 compared with the complete operative text on s2 pages 2–3

claims.text: Government Operations, consulting with the Governor's Office of Emergency Services and national experts, must submit recommendations by 16 November 2026.

The specified recommendation topics are onsite IVOs for large frontier developers, independent verification of required filings, an independently verified frontier-model kill switch and broader critical-safety-incident definitions.
The order does not itself impose those four requirements on developers; it directs officials to submit recommendations on the feasibility and efficacy of potential amendments to state law.
claims.sourceLocator: PDF pages 2–3, operative paragraph 3 and subparagraphs

claims.text: SB 813 creates IVO designation criteria addressing expertise, assessment methods, conflicts of interest, operational independence, documentation and cybersecurity.
SB 813 does not require a developer, deployer or operator to engage an IVO or undergo a covered audit as a condition of operating in California.
AB 1405 creates an auditor registry, audit-reporting and recordkeeping duties, independence rules and a misconduct-reporting path.
IVO designation or auditor registration is not evidence that a particular model passed an independent safety review.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: the schemes govern assessor designation, registration and conduct; SB 813 section 8898.4 excludes state endorsement and mandatory engagement. Conclusion is bounded Index Us synthesis.

claims.text: Independent reporting describes the kill switch and related measures as proposals to be explored rather than obligations imposed now.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 opening and governor ambiguity passage; s6 opening, recommendations and legislative follow-through passages

claims.text: Because kill switch can refer to controls at different system layers, a useful rule must define its scope, trigger authority, safe state, verification method and restoration conditions.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s2 orders a technical-feasibility and efficacy assessment with ongoing verification; s5 reports the governor's acknowledgement that the term has multiple meanings. Control requirements are Index Us synthesis.

claims.text: Developers can prepare without assuming a final rule by mapping emergency controls, triggers, evidence, dependencies, testing and restoration conditions.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: imminent recommendation deadline and earlier assessor-framework implementation. Recommendation is Index Us operational synthesis.

claims.text: The 16 November recommendations are the next public evidence needed to assess the proposal's technical scope and route to enforceability.
claims.sourceLocator: Based on the order's explicit report deadline and the absence of a current developer mandate; later legislative action remains uncertain.
